title: Tuple vs List Mutability
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Robotics and Computational Thinking
description: A side-by-side mutation test that runs the same operation on a list and a tuple holding the same robot data (motor pins, an RGB color, or the OLED size). Changes work on the list, while the tuple refuses with the real MicroPython TypeError or AttributeError.

learningObjectives: Distinguish the operations that work on both lists and tuples (reading and looping) from those that work only on lists (changing, appending, removing).
Predict the TypeError or AttributeError a tuple raises when code tries to change it.
Choose a tuple for fixed hardware values and a list for data that grows.
prerequisites: Creating lists and reading items by index
standards: CSTA 2-AP-11: Create clearly named variables that represent different data types and perform operations on their values

pedagogical.interactionPattern: Students choose a data set and an operation, then run it on a list and a tuple at the same time and compare the two results.
keyQuestions: Which operations work on both a list and a tuple?
What error do you get when you try to change a tuple?
Why is a tuple a good choice for motor pin numbers?
Which robot data should be a list instead?
commonMisconceptions: Tuples cannot be read or looped over because they cannot be changed.
A tuple can be changed with append() like a list.
Whether data can change depends on the values stored, not the type of container.
assessmentOpportunities: Prediction table for five operations on a list and a tuple.
Challenge: choose tuple or list for the OLED size and the last ten distance readings.
Exit ticket: explain why fixed values in config.py benefit from being unchangeable.
